source: NCERT Class VII, Exploring Society: India and Beyond, Geography Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Weather and Climate
points: **Weather** = the state of the atmosphere at a place over a **short period** (day to day).
**Climate** = the **average of weather** over a **long period** (many years).
Weather can change quickly; climate is fairly constant for a region.

sections.heading: 2. Elements of Weather
points: **Temperature** — hotness/coldness of air; measured by a **thermometer** (°C).
**Air pressure** — weight of air; measured by a **barometer**.
**Humidity** — amount of **water vapour** in the air; measured by a **hygrometer**.
**Wind** — moving air; direction shown by a **wind vane**, speed by an **anemometer**.
**Precipitation (rainfall)** — rain/snow/hail; measured by a **rain gauge**.
**Cloud cover / sunshine** are also elements.

sections.heading: 3. What Controls the Weather
points: The **Sun** is the main source of heat; temperature depends on **latitude, altitude and time of day**.
**Winds** bring moisture and change temperature; **water bodies** moderate temperature.
**Water cycle** processes (evaporation, condensation) produce clouds and rain.

sections.heading: 4. Reading and Forecasting Weather
points: Weather is observed at **weather stations** and by **satellites**.
In India, the **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** records and **forecasts** weather.
Forecasts help in **farming, travel, fishing and disaster warnings** (cyclones, heavy rain).

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Weather = short-term; climate = long-term average.
Instruments: thermometer (temperature), barometer (pressure), hygrometer (humidity), anemometer (wind speed), wind vane (direction), rain gauge (rainfall).
Sun = main source of heat; temperature depends on latitude/altitude.
IMD = India Meteorological Department (records & forecasts weather).
Forecasts aid farming, travel, fishing and disaster warnings.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Weather = short-term**; **climate = long-term** — the most common mix-up.
**Hygrometer** measures **humidity**; **anemometer** measures **wind speed** — don't swap with a barometer/thermometer.
**Rainfall** is measured by a **rain gauge**.
**IMD** is India's official weather agency.
